arxiv-1701-03135.title: Guaranteed recovery of quantum processes from few measurements
arxiv-1701-03135.creator: M. Kliesch, R. Kueng, J. Eisert, D. Gross
arxiv-1701-03135.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by M. Kliesch, R. Kueng, J. Eisert, D. Gross. Quantum process tomography is the task of reconstructing unknown quantum channels from measured data. In this work, we introduce compressed sensing-based methods that facilitate the reconstruction of quantum channels of low Kraus rank. Our main contribution is the analysis of a natural measurement model for this task: We assume that data is obtained by sending pure states into the channel and measuring expectation values on the output.

arxiv-2104-12939.title: Provably Convergent Learned Inexact Descent Algorithm for Low-Dose CT Reconstruction
arxiv-2104-12939.creator: Qingchao Zhang, Mehrdad Alvandipour, Wenjun Xia, Yi Zhang, Xiaojing Ye, Yunmei Chen
arxiv-2104-12939.description: Abstract We propose a provably convergent method, called Efficient Learned Descent Algorithm (ELDA), for low-dose CT (LDCT) reconstruction. ELDA is a highly interpretable neural network architecture with learned parameters and meanwhile retains convergence guarantee as classical optimization algorithms. To improve reconstruction quality, the proposed ELDA also employs a new non-local feature mapping and an associated regularizer.

arxiv-2206-01776.title: Properties of a Ternary Infinite Word
arxiv-2206-01776.creator: James Currie, Pascal Ochem, Narad Rampersad, Jeffrey Shallit
arxiv-2206-01776.description: Abstract We study the properties of the ternary infinite word 𝐩 = 012102101021012101021012 ⋯ , {\bf p}=012102101021012101021012\cdots, that is, the fixed point of the map h : 0 → 01 h:0\rightarrow 01 , 1 → 21 1\rightarrow 21 , 2 → 0 2\rightarrow 0 . We determine its factor complexity, critical exponent, and prove that it is 2 2 -balanced.

arxiv-2502-07250.creator: Liying Han liying98@g.ucla.edu, Gaofeng Dong gfdong@g.ucla.edu, Xiaomin Ouyang xmouyang@cse.ust.hk, Kang Yang kyang73@g.ucla.edu, Lance Kaplan lance.m.kaplan.civ@army.mil, Federico Cerutti federico.cerutti@unibs.it, Mani Srivastava mbs@ucla.edu
arxiv-2502-07250.description: Abstract Modern machine learning models excel at detecting individual actions, sounds, or scene attributes from short, localized observations. However, many real-world tasks, such as in smart cities and healthcare, require reasoning over high-level complex events ( CE s): spatiotemporal, rule-governed patterns of short-term atomic events ( AE s).

Basque, J. Bateman, O. Benevides Rodrigues, S. Berkman, A. Bhat, M. Bhattacharya, M. Bishai, A. Blake, B. Bogart, T. Bolton, M. B. Brun
arxiv-2502-10900.description: Abstract We present MicroBooNE’s first search for dark sector e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} explanations of the long-standing MiniBooNE anomaly. arxiv-2506-08916.title: Enhancing generalizability of model discovery across parameter space with multi-experiment equation learning (ME-EQL)
arxiv-2506-08916.creator: Maria-Veronica Ciocanel, John T. Nardini, Kevin B. Flores, Erica M. Rutter, Suzanne S. Sindi, Alexandria Volkening
arxiv-2506-08916.description: Abstract Agent-based modeling (ABM) is a powerful tool for understanding self-organizing biological systems, but it is computationally intensive and often not analytically tractable. Equation learning (EQL) methods can derive continuum models from ABM data, but they typically require extensive simulations for each parameter set, raising concerns about generalizability.

arxiv-2511-18566.title: Effect of subgrid-scale anisotropy on wall-modeled large-eddy simulation of separated flow
arxiv-2511-18566.creator: Di Zhou 1,2, H. Jane Bae 1
arxiv-2511-18566.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Di Zhou 1,2, H. Jane Bae 1. We examine the role of anisotropic subgrid-scale (SGS) stress in wall-modeled large-eddy simulation (WMLES) of flow over a spanwise-uniform Gaussian-shaped bump, with particular emphasis on predicting flow separation. The simulations show that eddy-viscosity-based SGS models often yield non-monotonic predictions of the mean separation bubble size on the leeward side under grid refinement, whereas models incorporating anisotropic SGS stress produce more consistent results across mesh resolutions.
